title: In Search of Lost Domain Generalization
publication_status_observed: arXiv preprint arXiv:2007.01434v1 [cs.LG] 2 Jul 2020; listed as 'Preprint. Under review' in the paper
main_claims: Model selection is a non-trivial and often neglected component of domain generalisation research, and algorithms without a specified model selection strategy are incomplete.
When carefully implemented with modern neural architectures and data augmentation, empirical risk minimisation (ERM) achieves state-of-the-art performance across all seven DomainBed datasets.
DomainBed provides a standardised testbed with seven datasets, nine algorithms, and three model selection criteria to enable rigorous and reproducible domain generalisation research.
methodology: The authors implement nine domain generalisation algorithms (including IRM, CORAL, GroupDRO, Mixup, MLDG, DANN, CDANN, VREx, and ERM) under a unified framework with standardised architectures (ResNet-50 backbone), data augmentation, and hyperparameter search (random search, 20 trials). Three model selection criteria are evaluated: training-domain validation, leave-one-domain-out cross-validation, and oracle test-domain validation. Experiments cover VLCS, PACS, Office-Home, TerraIncognita, DomainNet, RotatedMNIST, and ColoredMNIST.
key_results: ERM with modern architecture and augmentation matches or outperforms more complex DG algorithms on all seven DomainBed datasets under fair comparison conditions.
On PACS, the authors' ERM achieves 85.7% average accuracy, surpassing the previous best published result of 84.5% (Asadi et al., 2019).
Model selection criterion has a large effect on reported performance, with oracle selection often inflating apparent gains of complex algorithms.
limitations: The study does not include flatness-oriented optimisers such as SAM or SWA, so implications for the role of loss landscape geometry are indirect.
Using a fixed ResNet-50 backbone may limit conclusions about algorithm-specific inductive biases.
The paper is a benchmark/re-evaluation study; it proposes no new DG algorithm.
relevance_to_rq: DomainBed provides the standard evaluation framework and datasets for domain generalisation benchmarking. While the RQ focuses on CIFAR-C corruptions rather than multi-domain DG, this paper establishes that fair comparison methodology and model selection are critical—a lesson that applies to evaluating SAM vs. SWA on CIFAR-C. ERM as a strong baseline also grounds the RQ's experimental design.
